thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Increased 5xx rate in eu-west-1 beginning ~1830499800. Traffic spillover observed to us-east-1. Potential misrouting to low-tier fallback models. Paging @oncall (Alex K).
Alex K: On it — grabbing pager. any known deploys?
Maya P: I'm seeing spike in requests that should route to 'rwd-large-v2' but a subset got routed to 'rwd-quant-fast' (lower precision). Could explain customer complaints about hallucinations.
Liam R: Which policy caused fallback? Is this the new tier-demotion policy rolled last week?
Maya P: Looks like the routing fabric hit a capacity threshold in eu-west-1 and the routing decision fell through to the 'fallback-model' set for "tier=standard". But many requests actually had header tier=premium.
Sarah G: Paging history shows config change 1830496000 by liam.r for emergency thundering-buffer — revert?
Alex K: Immediate mitigation: change routing priority to prefer region-local replicas and disable cross-region spillover for premium routes. I'll run the command.
Alex K: Running:
```
# set routing.policy.spillover.enabled=false --scope=premium --region=eu-west-1
redwoodctl routing update --policy spillover --region eu-west-1 --tier premium --set enabled=false
```
Maya P: I see the rocker config still had an older mapping for 'tier' -> 'fallback-set'. The mapping file had a missing override for 'premium' so it fell back.
devops-bot: Deploy started by Alex K (1830500123). Rolling update: routing-policy-service v1.14.3 -> v1.14.4
Liam R: Quick check: can we set a temporary rule to map any request with header `x-customer-tier: premium` to an explicit route?
Maya P: Yes. I can patch the router ruleset. Pushing patch now.
Maya P: Patch applied: `ruleset/prefer-local-premium` — currently in effect.
devops-bot: Rule activation confirmed (1830500345).
Sarah G: Customer impact: ticket stream shows 12 customer escalations (mostly high-priority) in last 20m, mostly from EU-based customers. Notifying CS.
Alex K: Logging snapshot of one misrouted request:
```
REQUEST ID: 9f3b2a
headers: {"x-region":"eu-west-1","x-customer-tier":"premium","x-model-preference":"rwd-large-v2"}
routing_decision: fallback_set=rwd-quant-fast, selected_host=us-east-1:gpu-21
cache_hit: false
latency_ms: 2100
```
Maya P: That matches — tier header was present but the routing map was ignored due to rule precedence bug. Hypothesis: recent change to `rule-evaluation-order` made generic fallback rules supersede explicit tier mappings.
Liam R: Reproduced locally: when rule-evaluation-order = "earliest-wins" and a generic fallback rule exists with earlier creation timestamp, it wins. We changed order to "priority-wins" in the new release but the config wasn't applied consistently.
Alex K: For mitigation, we reverted rule-evaluation-order to stable and pinned the premium mapping. Monitoring now.
devops-bot: Revert completed (1830500560).
Maya P: Can we collect a timeline for RCA? I'll start a thread skeleton:
- 1830496000 config change: emergency thundering-buffer by liam.r
- 1830499800 first error spikes reported by monitoring
- 1830500000 incident-bot alert/paging
- 1830500123 routing policy deploy by Alex K (partial)
- 1830500345 ruleset activation patch by Maya P
- 1830500560 revert of rule-eval-order by Alex K
- 1830500800 secondary mitigation: explicit premium mapping pinned

Sarah G: Adding customer impact timeline:
- 1830499900 first customer report via support (escalation-45)
- 1830500200 CS posted customer advisory to affected accounts
- 1830500500 temporary mitigation announced to customers

Liam R: Hypotheses list (in-thread):
1) misconfig: rule-evaluation-order change not uniformly applied -> generic fallback winning (High confidence)
2) model catalog mapping missing override for 'premium' in eu-west-1 (Medium)
3) KV cache mismatch between routing nodes causing stale mapping (Low)
4) race during routing-service rolling update -> partial config mix (Medium-High)

Maya P: Evidence so far: config diff, local repro of rule ordering, logs showing fallback rule timestamp earlier than premium mapping. That strongly supports hypothesis 1 and 4.
Alex K: For immediate post-incident actions: 1) Reconcile rule-eval-order rollout across regions. 2) Add test in CI to validate tier mappings after routing-service deploy. 3) Add alert for cross-region spillover percentage > 5% for premium routes.
Sarah G: CS action items: outreach to the 12 affected customers and offer credits + incident summary once RCA done.
Liam R: We should collect full log dump and upload to shared drive. I'll run the query and paste summary.
Liam R: Log query (snippet):
```
SELECT request_id, region, routing_decision, config_snapshot_ts
FROM routing_logs
WHERE timestamp BETWEEN 1830499800 AND 1830500600
AND routing_decision LIKE '%fallback%'
LIMIT 500;
```
Liam R: Uploading results to: https://internal.redwood/links/routing-logs-183050 (access: incident-team)
Maya P: Adding RCA tracker card: https://boards.redwood/rca/183050-routing-fallback-cascade (assigned: Liam R, Alex K, Maya P)
Alex K: On-call handoff plan: I'll stay on until 1830503600 then hand to Liam for postmortem work.
Sarah G: Noted. I'll prep the customer advisory template and coordinate CS responses.
devops-bot: Postmortem template created: /templates/incident_rca.md (1830500705)
Alex K: Confirming monitoring: Dropped error rate from 7.8% -> 0.6% after revert. Keep watch for 30m.
Maya P: Next steps for RCA write-up: root cause: inconsistent rollout of rule-evaluation-order causing fallback precedence; related contributing factor: missing mapping override in catalog for 'premium' in eu-west-1; actionables: rollout reconciliation, CI tests, monitoring alerts, catalog validation.
Liam R: I'll capture timeline and attach logs to RCA. Assigning follow-ups in tracker.
Sarah G: Customer comms ready to send once RCA draft is reviewed.
Alex K: Closing incident channel when error stays <1% for 30m. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
